methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Path Power operates in the Climate & Energy sector at an undisclosed stage. The comparable universe consists of one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. This limited public representation and fragmented private peer set reflect the early-stage, capital-intensive nature of frontier climate technology.

Standard peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow comparables. The analysis identified zero same-stage peers, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-tier private companies meeting screening criteria. While eight Climate & Energy companies populate the broader sector, none satisfied the minimum threshold of three datapoints within the same valuation tier and development stage. An all-sector median approach would introduce substantial methodological error given the heterogeneity in business models, capital requirements, and commercialization timelines across climate tech verticals.

Without triangulation via peer multiples, valuation synthesis is constrained. The analyst would need to pursue alternative methods—discounted cash flow analysis (if revenue/cost projections exist), venture capital method benchmarking, or transaction comps—to establish a defensible range. Key uncertainties include Path Power's revenue maturity, cash burn profile, and technical risk profile relative to the named peers. The sparse comparable set underscores the challenge of valuing pre-revenue or early-revenue frontier-tech ventures in fragmented sectors.
